name: Group

examples.title: Basic Usage
examples.code: Last saved a minute ago

examples.title: Toolbar
examples.code:
<Group justifyContent="space-between">
  <Title as="h2" size="4">
    Invoices
  </Title>
  <Group gap="1">
    <Button>Export</Button>
    <Button color="primary">New invoice</Button>
  </Group>
</Group>

accessibility:
- **No role of its own:** a Group adds nothing to the accessibility tree, apart from `role="list"`
  on a `ul` or `ol`, which Safari otherwise drops once Bulma's reset hides the markers.
- **Order:** it's a row in the children's own order, or a column below its `breakpoint` in the same
  order, so what's seen, the reading order and the Tab order agree at every width. Right to left,
  the row runs right to left.
- **Reflow:** it wraps by default, so a row of controls doesn't make the page scroll sideways at a
  width of 320 CSS pixels (WCAG 1.4.10).
- **Grouping controls:** a Group of buttons isn't announced as a group. When the buttons belong
  together and need a name, give it `role="group"` and an `aria-label`, or render it
  `as="fieldset"` with one.
summary: The `Group` component lays its children out in a row that wraps, centered on each other, with half of Bulma's block spacing between them. Use it for a row of buttons, tags or avatars beside some text, or a toolbar with `justifyContent="space-between"` pushing its ends apart. The children's own block margins are zeroed, so the gap is the only space. With `breakpoint`, it's a column on narrow screens and a row from that breakpoint up. For controls joined into one, with no gap and shared borders, use `hasAddons` on Field or Buttons instead.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render. With `ul` or `ol`, give it `li` children: it restates `role="list"`, which Bulma's list reset takes away in Safari.

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, a step of Bulma's gap scale. Unset, it's `--bulma-stack-horizontal-gap`, half of Bulma's block spacing.

props.name: alignItems
props.description: How each child sits across the row. While `breakpoint` stacks them, it's where each sits across the column.

props.name: justifyContent
props.description: Where the children sit along the row: `'space-between'` pushes the ends apart.

props.name: flexWrap
props.description: Whether children move to a new row when they don't fit.

props.name: isFullwidth
props.description: The children share the row equally, and fill the column while `breakpoint` stacks them (Bulma's `is-fullwidth`).

props.name: breakpoint
props.description: Stacks the children below this Bulma breakpoint and sets them in a row from it up, the breakpoints Container's `breakpoint` takes. Unset, a row at every width.

props.name: children
props.description: What it lays out. The top and bottom margins Bulma gives them are zeroed, so `gap` is the only space between them, and a spacing helper such as `mt="2"` still adds to it. A `Columns` child keeps its own top and side margins, and takes at the bottom the one Bulma gives the last Columns in a container, the column gap pulled back in (none when gapless), so its columns line up.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the element `as` renders.

parts.catchAll: Remaining props of the element selected by as and Bulma helper props

types.name: BulmaGapStep
types.summary: A gap step as `gap`, `columnGap` and `rowGap` take it: a value from `validGaps`, or the same step written as a number (`gap={2}`, `gap={1.5}`). `Grid` took its gaps as numbers before the gap helpers were shared, so every gap prop still does.

types.name: LayoutElement
types.summary: The elements Stack, Group, Center and Flex can render as: Container's landmarks and sections, a list, a form or a fieldset.
